ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition.issue: RE-CLOSED 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13, R5 fix pass) -- verdict unchanged, MECHANISM replaced. The abstention on an Exhaust-keyword card is no longer a sim-specific second test: the Play pile made _resolve_card_play pass this hook GetResultPileTypeForCardPlay's REAL answer (CardModel.cs:2070-2082 as :1890's defaultPileType), so an exhausting play arrives already seeded 'exhaust' and C#'s ONE guard -- `if (pileType != PileType.Discard) return (pileType, position);`, ReboundPower.cs:25-28 -- covers it. The explicit `card.exhausts or card.exhaust_on_next_play` re-test the previous close describes is DELETED, and so is the older `card not in player.discard_pile` Play-limbo test, WHICH THE REAL play_pile MADE FALSE FOR EVERY CARD AT HOOK TIME and which would have silently retired this power. WHAT REASONING THIS REPLACES: that the sim's hook 'always receives the literal discard, so the test has to be made here'. It no longer does.  The text it replaced read: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13): FIXED (2026-08-01, incl. the fix-pass correction). The pile decision moved onto modify_card_play_result_pile, matching ReboundPower.cs:19-30 and CardModel.cs:1890's timing. THE FIRST PASS WAS PREMATURE and the review caught it: as originally shipped the power still ticked and redirected an Exhaust-keyword card, where GetResultPileTypeForCardPlay (CardModel.cs:2070-2083) seeds the chain with PileType.Exhaust and ReboundPower.cs:25-28 abstains on any non-Discard seed -- live via Trash Heap Rebound plus any of 36 exhausting cards and invisible to every test. The shipped guard now abstains identically (re-derived arm-for-arm by the reviewer against every seed C# can produce; the only uncovered arm is IsDupe, unmodelled engine-wide). The reasoning replaced: that the sim's collapsed on_card_played placement was observably equivalent.  The text it replaced read: The destination-pile DECISION is replaced by an after-the-fact move. The sim has the matching hook -- hooks.modify_card_play_result_pile (hooks.py:236-246), dispatched at combat.py:510 -- and this power does not use it, reaching into the piles from on_card_played (combat.py:514) instead. Because combat.py:510 runs FIRST, NostalgiaPower (powers.py:3595-3612), which does use the hook, can move the card to the top of the draw pile before this power looks for it in the discard pile, at which point this power's `card in discard_pile` test fails and it silently does nothing -- neither its effect nor its stack consumption. In C# both are listeners on ONE ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition chain (Hook.cs:1391-1405) and the last writer wins, so both always get a say. Which one wins in C# is hook_dispatch G2's listener-order question and is not re-verdicted here. Both powers are ported Ironclad-pool content, so the contention is reachable. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Rebound is the sharper case of the pair, because Nostalgia and Rebound BOTH want the discard -> draw-top redirect: in C# they contend on one chain and one of them wins; in the sim Nostalgia runs first at combat.py:510, moves the card, and Rebound then finds nothing in the discard pile -- so Rebound gets its effect for free and, worse, never consumes its stack (powers.py:2794's _tick is inside the `card in discard_pile` branch). A Rebound stack therefore survives a play Nostalgia handled, where in C# exactly one AfterModifyingCardPlayResultPileOrPosition fires.
